scenes.say: Why do system designers love queues and publish-subscribe? How do they make async processing reliable?

scenes.label: Queue
scenes.sub: Decouples producers and consumers for background tasks.
scenes.say: A queue decouples producers from consumers. It lets you process tasks in the background, at your own pace.
Queues send each message to one consumer. Publish-subscribe, or pub-sub, lets many consumers get the same message.

rows.b: Move failed jobs to a special queue
Make sure repeats don't cause errors

scenes.say: To handle failures, retry jobs, use a dead-letter queue for stubborn ones, and design your logic to be idempotent. That means repeated processing won't break things.

scenes.question: What if retries aren't idempotent?
scenes.right: You risk duplicate side effects, like double billing. Always make retries safe.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: If your retries aren't idempotent, you could double-charge a user or trigger duplicate actions. Always make retries safe.
